title: Presence of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Organomineral Fertilizer
author: Glauco Mariano Teixeira Junior
materials: QIAGEN® DNeasy® PowerSoil® Pro Figure 1. DNeasy PowerSoil Pro Kit.

Gently mix the contents of the tubes by stirring, then place the reaction tubes in the thermocycler, following specific settings for Tet and antibiotic-resistant genes listed in Table 1 and Table 2 . Figure 8. 0.2 mL strip tubes with PCR reaction being placed in the thermocycler.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Lysis
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the organomineral fertilizer using a bead-beating process.

substeps.instruction: Measure 250 mg of organomineral fertilizer.
Add the fertilizer and 800 µL of Solution CD1 to PowerBead Pro tubes.
Vortex the sample in the Bead Beater for 45 seconds at max speed, ensuring tubes are balanced and the lid is closed.
Centrifuge tubes at 15,000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: DNA Purification
steps.instruction: Purify the lysate using a series of wash and elution steps.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 500 µL - 600 µL of supernatant to a new 2 mL Microcentrifuge Tube.
Add 200 µL Solution CD2 and vortex for 5 seconds.
Centrifuge at 15,000 x g for 1 minute and transfer 700 µL of supernatant to a new tube.
Add 600 µL Solution CD3 and vortex for 5 seconds.
Repeat the process for any remaining lysate.
Transfer 650 µL lysate to MB Spin Column, centrifuge at 15,000 x g for 1 minute, and discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL Solution EA, centrifuge at 15,000 x g for 1 minute, and discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL Solution C5, centrifuge at 15,000 x g for 1 minute, discard flow-through, and centrifuge again for 2 minutes.
Elute DNA by adding 100 µL Solution C6 to the filter and centrifuging at 15,000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: DNA Storage
steps.instruction: Store the extracted DNA at -30 °C with a unique recognizable identifier.

steps.title: PCR Reaction Setup
steps.instruction: Prepare PCR reactions in 0.2 mL strip tubes using the following components:

substeps.instruction: Mix 12.5 µL Master Mix JumpStart Red Taq (P0982-800rxn), 5.5 µL PCR Water, 1 µL Forward Primer (10 µM), 1 µL Reverse Primer (10 µM), and 5 µL DNA Sample.
For negative control: replace DNA sample with PCR Water.
For positive control: replace DNA sample with gBlock variety.

Prepare specific gBlock positive controls: tetA (1 µL gBlock 12 + 4 µL PCR water), tetX (2 µL gBlock 10 + 3 µL PCR water), and for tetO (gBlock 13), ermB (gBlock 17), intI1 (gBlock 19), bla CTX-M-32 (gBlock 18), and sul 1 (gBlock 3), use 3 µL gBlock + 2 µL PCR water.

steps.title: Agarose Gel Preparation
steps.instruction: Cast an agarose gel for electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 0.4 g of agarose and 50 mL of 1x TAE buffer in an Erlenmeyer Flask and mix gently.
Cover the flask with a paper towel and microwave for 30 seconds until the solution bubbles; repeat if necessary until clear.
Using thermal gloves, add 2 µL ethidium bromide (for tetA, tetX, tetO) or 4 µL SYBR safe (for ermB, intI1, bla CTX-M-32, sul 1).
Pour the mixture into a gel casting tray with the gel comb in place.
Allow the gel to cool to room temperature until solidified.

steps.title: Gel Electrophoresis and Analysis
steps.instruction: Run the PCR amplicons on the gel and analyze the results.

substeps.instruction: Place the gel and casting tray into the Gel Electrophoresis Apparatus.
Add 0.25x TAE buffer to the tank until the gel is fully submerged.
Load 10 µL of the PCR amplicon into the 40 µl gel wells.
Run the gel at 130 V for 30 minutes.
Analyze the gel under UV light (using eye protection) to detect DNA bands.
